source: TensorRT-LLM VisualGen self-golden (not a cross-stack reference)
what_this_gates: Drift in the static-FP8 (ModelOpt-calibrated, per-tensor) load and execution path. It is deliberately NOT referenced against BF16: diffusion sampling is chaotic, so an FP8 rounding difference at step 0 compounds into a different but equally valid sample, and a BF16-referenced threshold would either reject good FP8 output or be too loose to catch anything. Measured FP8-vs-BF16 LPIPS at 704x1280/20 steps is 0.025 (T2I) to 0.175 (T2V) -- far above any useful gate.
prompt: A serene mountain landscape with snow-capped peaks and a flowing river
cheap_by_design: 256x256 is the smallest legal resolution (VAE spatial factor 16 x latent patch size 2 => multiples of 32) and 4 steps is enough to move the sample clear of the initial noise. The gate only has to run every quantized projection in every layer once; it is not judging image quality, so it does not need the deployed 720x1280/35-step shape. That is ~14x fewer patches and ~9x fewer steps than the sibling Cosmos3 goldens.
reproducibility: Two independent renders on one B300 (sm_103, TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc24) under deterministic algorithms were bit-identical: LPIPS 0.000000, max pixel delta 0. The threshold is therefore entirely headroom for cross-host kernel drift, matching the ~0.04 the sibling Cosmos3 goldens allow for.
topology_guard: The generator asserts at least one GatedMLP has gate_up_proj is None before rendering. Static FP8 splits gate/up to preserve each projection's calibrated scale; if it ever silently reverted to the fused topology the image would differ only subtly, the test would still pass, and regenerating the golden in that state would enshrine the re-quantized weights this feature exists to avoid. Observed 72 split GatedMLPs (36 layers x 2 towers) on Cosmos3-Nano-FP8.
